answer: One concrete defense is to make identity costly and reputation earned rather than minted. Each agent posts a refundable bond at the network wharf before it can act, and every action it takes carries a peer-attested signal of prior honest work. A sybil operator must fund a whole dune of separate bonds to gain comparable weight, while a genuine agent amortizes one stake across a long verifiable history, so forged crowds cost strictly more than the influence they can ever buy.
